Definition: from a (presumed) derivative of βδέω (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry):--abhor, abominable.
BiblicalUsage: Bdelysso means to abhor, to detest, to turn away in disgust, and Paul asks the man who abhors idols whether he commits sacrilege, while John lists the abominable among those whose part is in the lake of fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that abhorring idols is only honest when the life matches the hatred, and Paul's question still catches everyone who hates the sin and loves its profit.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
